name: Deep ITM Short Put
summary: Sell a put that is already well in the money to collect a large credit. Mostly a bad idea: near-certain assignment for very little extrinsic value.
max_profit: The extrinsic portion of the credit only - typically a small fraction of the large premium received
max_loss: (strike - credit) x 100. Similar downside to owning the stock, with all upside capped at the strike.
breakevens: strike - credit, usually near or below current spot

greeks.theta: positive but small in dollars (little extrinsic to decay)

when_to_use: Rarely. The only defensible use is as a cheaper-to-execute synthetic equivalent of a deep ITM covered call when the call side has a worse market. Otherwise it accepts stock-like downside for a bond-like return with near-certain assignment.
entry_rules: Extrinsic value = credit - max(0, strike - spot); require extrinsic >= 0.6% of strike per 30 days, otherwise there is no return at all
Bid/ask <= 4% of mid - deep ITM put markets are wide
Flag as LOW PRIORITY: in almost every case a -0.25 delta CSP or a deep ITM covered call offers better risk-adjusted terms
management_rules: Close at 60% of the available extrinsic, not 60% of the total credit - the intrinsic portion is not profit
Roll down and out for a net credit if delta exceeds -0.92
Do not hold for the last 14 days; the remaining extrinsic does not pay for the assignment risk
exit_rules: Close at 60% of extrinsic captured or at 14 DTE, whichever first

NEVER-ASSIGN RULE, tightened because the position is ITM by design: close immediately whenever extrinsic value falls below $0.05, whenever delta exceeds -0.92, and unconditionally by 14:00 ET on expiration day. Backstop 15:45 ET
Early assignment probability here is materially higher than for OTM puts because deep ITM puts lose extrinsic quickly and carry an interest-rate-driven early exercise incentive
assignment_risk: VERY HIGH by construction. Assignment delivers 100 shares at a strike above the market - an immediate paper loss equal to the intrinsic value, offset by the credit already received.
liquidity_needs: Wide markets are the norm; reject above 4% of mid.
common_mistakes: Mistaking the large credit for a large profit - only the extrinsic is ever earned; underestimating how quickly interest-rate-driven early exercise hits deep ITM short puts.
